name: capstone core disassembly engine
description:
HARNESS RULES FOR THIS GROUP: (a) the MAIN PATH below runs on every input with the full input, exactly as listed; it is the baseline, the rest of this Logic Group only adds to it. (b) Entries marked 'same core / alternative' reach the same internal code as the main call: never replace the main call with them and never run all of them on every input (fan-out kills exec/s); if used, run at most one of them as an extra step chosen by spare input bits. (c) A configuration switch must never take inputs away from the main path; options that only add code (e.g. detail/verbose output) stay ON. (d) This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers, tests and examples do with the target stays in scope.
MAIN PATH (keep on every input; verified in capstonev5 source):
1. cs_open(arch, mode) with (arch, mode) picked by one input byte from a broad table of every compiled-in architecture/mode combination (the project's own table suite/fuzz/platform.c lists ~50: X86 16/32/64, ARM/THUMB/THUMB+MCLASS/ARM+V8, ARM64, MIPS32/64/MICRO/MIPS32R6 BE+LE, PPC64 BE, SPARC/SPARC V9, SYSZ, XCORE, M68K, M680X, TMS320C64X, EVM, MOS65XX, WASM, BPF classic/extended, RISCV32/64, SH, TRICORE). A failing cs_open just returns.
2. cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_SYNTAX, s) with s taken from input bits. NOT cosmetic: on X86, CS_OPT_SYNTAX_ATT swaps handle->printer to X86_ATT_printInst (arch/X86/X86Module.c:61-90), a completely separate printer (X86ATTInstPrinter.c + the AT&T tables of X86GenAsmWriter.inc, the largest printer code in the project); INTEL/MASM keep the Intel printer with different output; ARM (ARMModule.c:55, ARM_getRegName) and PPC (PPCInstPrinter.c:1190) honour CS_OPT_SYNTAX_NOREGNAME; MOS65XX honours CS_OPT_SYNTAX_MOTOROLA (MOS65XXModule.c:64-73). All previous LG harnesses dropped this option and lost ~24 points of coverage.
3. cs_option(CS_OPT_DETAIL, CS_OPT_ON) on EVERY input (detail filling is a strict superset; not a 50% switch); CS_OPT_SKIPDATA and CS_OPT_UNSIGNED (and the no-op-on-v5 CS_OPT_NO_BRANCH_OFFSET) from input bits.
4. cs_disasm(handle, code, code_size, address, count, &insn) on the code bytes (address and count may come from input bytes, count 0 = all), then consume every instruction: mnemonic/op_str, cs_insn_name, and the detail arrays via cs_reg_name/cs_group_name; cs_free(insn, n).
5. cs_option(handle, CS_OPT_MODE, another mode of the SAME arch) (cs.c:824-829 validates it; X86_option switches regsize_map, ARM_option switches the ARM/Thumb decoder) and a second cs_disasm on the remaining bytes with the same handle; then cs_close(&handle).
ADDITIONS on top of 1-5 (spare input bits only): cs_disasm_iter (same core / alternative: run it as an extra pass, never instead of cs_disasm), CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP callback, cs_regs_access/cs_insn_group/cs_reg_read/cs_op_count/cs_op_index on detail. CS_OPT_MNEMONIC hits a known stack overflow in str_replace (cs.c:556-567) quickly, so gate it behind a rare selector value instead of a whole bit.

FEATURE DESCRIPTION (from the Logic Group stage):
cs_disasm is Capstone's main entry point: given a handle configured by cs_open/cs_option, it takes an untrusted raw byte buffer (machine code) plus an address/offset and count, and decodes it into an array of cs_insn structures, dynamically growing an internal cache. It repeatedly calls the architecture-specific decoder (handle->disasm, e.g. X86_getInstruction), the architecture printer (handle->printer) and insn_id mapper, then fill_insn to finish formatting mnemonic/operand strings and copy raw bytes into the public cs_insn, optionally allocating a cs_detail structure per instruction. On a decode failure it can "skip data" (skipdata_size/skipdata_opstr/user skipdata callback) and keep going, which is itself a distinct code path worth fuzzing. This function and its siblings directly parse attacker-controlled bytes across many architectures/parsers, so it is the primary security boundary of the whole project (malformed instruction encodings, operand decoding, buffer-length handling, cache growth/realloc logic are all exercised here).
- cs_disasm: target, decodes a full buffer in one call, core = decode loop, skipdata handling, fill_insn, detail allocation.
- cs_open: lifecycle/config, selects cs_arch/cs_mode (e.g. CS_ARCH_X86/ARM/ARM64/MIPS/... combined with CS_MODE_32/64/THUMB/BIG_ENDIAN/etc.) which installs the handle->disasm/printer/insn_id function pointers that cs_disasm calls — this choice is the single biggest driver of which internal decoder/printer code runs.
- cs_option: config, called before/after cs_open to toggle CS_OPT_DETAIL (enables cs_detail allocation and the detail-filling code paths), CS_OPT_SKIPDATA (+CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP for a custom skip-size callback/mnemonic, exercising the "broken instruction" recovery branch in the decode loop), CS_OPT_UNSIGNED and CS_OPT_MNEMONIC (custom mnemonic linked list used inside fill_insn); reaches the same core as cs_disasm by changing its behavior.
- cs_disasm_iter: variant, single-step decode API that runs essentially the same per-instruction core (MCInst_Init, handle->disasm, handle->printer, fill_insn, skipdata) one instruction at a time instead of filling an array — same core, alternative call pattern that a harness can combine with cs_disasm on the same buffer.
- cs_malloc / cs_free: lifecycle helpers used together with cs_disasm_iter (cs_malloc allocates one cs_insn with optional detail matching handle->detail) and to release cs_disasm's output array.
- cs_regs_access / cs_insn_group / cs_reg_read / cs_reg_write / cs_op_count / cs_op_index: consumers that walk the cs_detail structure produced by cs_disasm when CS_OPT_DETAIL is on, exercising the detail/groups/operand arrays built during decoding for each architecture.
Input space to fuzz: (1) cs_arch/cs_mode passed to cs_open — this selects an entirely different decoder/printer/insn_id implementation (X86, ARM, ARM64, MIPS, PPC, SPARC, SYSZ, XCORE, M68K, TMS320C64X, M680X, EVM, RISCV, MOS65XX, WASM, BPF, SH, TRICORE) and is the most permissive dimension, running the most distinct core code; (2) the raw code buffer bytes/size/address/count given to cs_disasm — directly fuzzes the architecture decoder's instruction-length and operand parsing and the skipdata recovery path when bytes are invalid; (3) CS_OPT_DETAIL on/off — toggles the cs_detail allocation/fill code; (4) CS_OPT_SKIPDATA on + CS_OPT_SKIPDATA_SETUP with a custom callback/mnemonic — exercises the "broken instruction" skip-and-continue logic differently from the default per-arch skipdata_size; (5) count=0 (disassemble all) vs count>0 (stop early, also affects internal cache_size sizing). This list is incomplete; what the project's own fuzzers and tests do with the target stays.
